newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends down in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends down in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.07 down at 41.40 to the dollar on Thursday but is likely to open stable on Friday, dealers said.
"The dollar rose on higher demand but rupee sources are drying up, which may prompt traders to book profits in the dollar at these levels," one dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on May 6, was 40.3300/40.5317 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.40 percent, compared to Wednesday's close at 2.35 percent.
